All six runs pass every assertion: 4/4 for both vector-reserve configurations, 4/4 for both billing-flow configurations, and 5/5 for both leader-failover configurations. The aggregate 100% versus 100% result means no current assertion distinguishes skill behavior from this strong baseline.

The strengthened provenance assertions succeed across all three skill runs: implementation facts stay tied to the PR, motivation and evaluative framing stay tied to supplied context, contradictions are qualified, and unsupported claims are excluded or converted into questions. This confirms the desired provenance behavior, but the same assertions also pass all three baselines.

The skill outputs provide materially finer provenance than the binary grades expose. They define claim IDs such as P1-P3 and C1-C5 or I1-I6 and C1-C3, then attach those IDs to timed beats and individual storyboard scenes; the baselines generally use source-boundary prose or one source column without claim-level references.

Each provenance assertion bundles several requirements into one pass/fail result. Because both configurations satisfy the broad boundary, the benchmark cannot separately reveal differences in implementation-fact discipline, contextual attribution, contradiction handling, unsupported-claim suppression, or beat-level traceability.

Renderer selection remains non-discriminating: both configurations choose Manim for the two evolving-mechanism cases and Remotion for the screenshot-led billing case, and every renderer-rationale assertion passes.

Audience tuning, duration and branding, and the production/review ownership rules also pass in both configurations wherever tested. These checks confirm minimum correctness but provide no evidence of incremental skill value in this iteration.

The vector-reserve caption assertion still permits materially different deliverables: the skill supplies 13 cue-level timestamped captions, while the baseline passes with prose synchronization and split-point instructions. Production-ready caption granularity is not measured.

Leader-failover still lacks an explicit approval-gate assertion even though its prompt requires stopping for approval. Both outputs did stop, but that central behavior is visible only through manual inspection rather than the benchmark score.

Skill outputs total 40,691 characters versus 14,853 for baselines, about 2.7 times as much text, while pass rates remain equal. Much of the added material is the evidence ledger, beat-level provenance, detailed scene packet, and review contract, so the benchmark should measure those artifacts if the extra planning detail is intended value.

Resource comparisons remain incomplete: all runs report 0.0 seconds and four of six runs report zero tokens. The +2,748 mean-token delta is driven only by leader-failover (13,306 versus 5,061) and is not a reliable suite-wide cost estimate.
